newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 1.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:

* U.S. President Bill Clinton has decided to allow U.S. computer companies to export more powerful data scrambling software, but only if they set up a system that will enable keys to the code to be obtained by law enforcement officials. Vice President Al Gore is to announce the decision later this week.
* Republic Industries Inc abandoned its bid to acquire ADT Ltd for more than $4 billion in Republic stock.
* Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Connecticut agreed to merge with Anthem Inc.
* Big German companies like Daimler-Benz AG plan to cut back some of the most generous employee benefits in the world.
* U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accused Maricopa County, Arizona of securities fraud in relation to the 1993 sale of about $48 million in general obligation bonds.
* California Public Employee Retirement System and State Board of Administration of Florida criticized Archer Daniels Midland Co for its attempts to create a more independent board.
* August new home sales rose 4.7 percent, while personal income and personal consumption both rose six-tenths of a percent during the same month.
* Circulation at Detroit Free Press of Knight-Ridder Inc and Detroit News of Gannett Co Inc has fallen by more than 30 percent since the newspapers's workers went on strike in July 1995.
* Kiwi International Air Lines has filed for bankruptcy protection.

* National Association of Securities Dealers (NASDAQ) fined securities firm Alex Brown & Sons $100,000 and registered representatives Beaumont Bianchi $50,000 for violations committed while selling foreign securities.
* Sweden's Autovil AB announced it will merge with ASP of Morton International Inc.

* 104th Congress gave a select few investors an investment opportunity by expanding the powers of the Federal Agricultural Mortgage Association. The entity's class A stock soared 292 percent on the NASDAQ.
